## CEO overview

What is changing: Firstmate can now answer the captain inside the same phone conversation the captain wrote from.
  One new command sends a reply that is tied to one specific message the captain already sent, and there is still no way to start a conversation, write to anyone else, or push status to the phone.
Why it matters: The captain could already reach Firstmate from his phone, but Firstmate had no way to answer there, so every answer had to appear somewhere the captain was not looking.
Customer or business impact: The captain gets his answer where he asked the question, and every attempt is either proven delivered, reported as definitely not delivered, or reported as unclear, so an answer is never silently lost and never sent twice.
Risk and rollout: Medium.
  The reply is written down before it is sent and is only recorded as delivered when Telegram returns a response that ties back to that exact conversation, message, and text; a refusal, timeout, or crash never reads as delivered, and an unclear outcome is reported as unknown and is never retried on its own.
  Nothing switches on by merging: this branch does not arm or change the running home's live Telegram source, so rollout is the captain merging and then arming it deliberately.
  Synchronize this narrative into the live pull request description while preserving its machine-owned `## Pipeline` section.

## What changed technically

- Added `bin/fm-procevent-telegram.sh reply <accepted-inbound-update-id>`, with the reply body read from standard input only and no caller-supplied destination: the state engine derives the chat, sender, and `message_id` from the stored accepted inbound record, refuses records that cannot prove a reply target, and rejects blank or over-limit text before anything is reserved.
- Extended `bin/fm_procevent_telegram_state.py` with a `replies` table and one transactional reply per inbound update: it reserves durably before the network call, commits `sent` only on a validated response bound to that chat, message, and body, records a definite Telegram refusal as `definitely-failed`, and records transport, timeout, malformed, and crash outcomes as `delivery-unknown` with no automatic retry.
- Kept locally proven non-delivery (send-preparation failure, 401, 404, 429) as a pre-network reservation that stays owed across polls and age, naming the exact `reply <update-id>` to re-issue.
- Taught `doctor` to print per-state reply totals, every still-owed reservation, and a bounded newest set of terminal rows with a `reply_attention_omitted` count.
- Documented the command and its failure handling in `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, the `process-event-sources` skill, and the verification record, and covered the new paths in `tests/fm-procevent-telegram.test.sh`.
- Kept the latest base branch's 18-case snapshot compatibility suite bounded under stock macOS Bash by removing redundant full-line whitespace copies, allowing the retained large fixture enough scan time, and assigning the measured suite a 20-minute job budget.
- Added `.github/pr-bodies/22.md` so this pull request's required communication narrative is reviewable in the branch itself.

## Validation

Checks passed: The change's own suite `tests/fm-procevent-telegram.test.sh` passes 77 of 77 cases, and the pull request communication suite `tests/pr-communication.test.sh` passes 13 of 13.
  The real communication checker accepts this narrative combined with the machine-owned `## Pipeline` section, and the repository lint gate `bin/fm-lint.sh` and the documentation ownership check `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` both pass.
  On GitHub, run `33759495115` for head `0ce186a73e37401355924ce210c44fb601a17fbd` passes every check except the stock macOS Bash job, which is cancelled at its exact ten-minute limit without an assertion failure.
  Against a local latest-base fixture, the corrected workflow path passes all 18 snapshot assertions and all 43 Bearings assertions, while the focused decision-fold suite, its broader supervision consumers, ShellCheck, and all five workflow lints pass.
Checks not run: The corrected final head has not yet run on a hosted stock macOS Bash 3.2 runner, which is the remaining authoritative compatibility check.
Evidence and limitations: A fake Telegram service with durable conversation state was driven end to end through the shipped adapter, showing the captain's phone question answered in the same chat and threaded to his message, repeat attempts staying idempotent with no second network call, refusal of arbitrary or proactive destinations, loud refusal of an inbound record without reply identity, a transport failure surfacing as delivery unknown with retry refused, a rate limit leaving the reply owed with the exact command to re-issue, a definite refusal becoming durably failed, and no bot token or reply text in stored state, results, or output.
  The compatibility failure is a deadline mismatch exposed by the latest base branch's multi-megabyte fixture: stock Bash 3.2 repeatedly copied each 180 KB status line before parsing it, while the job still expected the former 15-case suite and allowed only ten minutes.
  The fix preserves all 18 assertions, the large transport fixture, and production timeout defaults, and final hosted execution remains the proof against macOS runner variance.
  Limitation: two residual behaviors are accepted rather than fixed here, namely Telegram's own text normalization and the counting unit of the 4096 character limit, either of which can turn a genuinely delivered reply into a permanently unretryable delivery-unknown row.

## Module-boundary decision

Module-boundary decision: Current modules retained.
  The send path lives in the existing transactional Telegram state engine and its shell adapter rather than in a new sender, so the credential snapshot, strict identity configuration, integrity checking, and doctor reporting stay in one owner.
  The consumer seam stays with the `process-event-sources` skill instruction and routes requirements through firstmate rather than editing the adapter.

## Decision needed

Decision needed: Yes.
  Merge authority was not granted for this delivery, so the captain decides whether to merge and when to arm the live Telegram source, and whether the two accepted residual behaviors named above are acceptable to ship as they are.
